findings.title: The low-rank SDP uses the wrong spectral scale and admits an unsafe point
findings.claim_scope: For rank(A)≤k and ||A||₂≤M, the displayed SDP is asserted to project to the exact robust one-step safe set.
findings.hypotheses_checked: Positive M and positive integer rank budget; all original state constraints and both signed scalar safety constraints retained in the example.
findings.proof: The printed PSD block [[MI,A],[Aᵀ,I]] is equivalent to AAᵀ≤MI, hence ||A||₂≤sqrt(M), not M. For n=k=1, M=4, S=[−1,1], x=1/2, each h=±1 admits alpha=0, eta1=1/8, eta3=1/2, eta2=−xh/2: the first PSD block vanishes; the second has eigenvalues 0 and 5/8; scalar cost M eta1+eta3=1. The true admissible A=4 sends x to2 outside S. True safe interval [−1/4,1/4], printed scalar projection [−1/2,1/2].
findings.decisive_calculation: Root exact rational computation checked complete displayed-program feasibility, PSD certificates and unsafe transition; general Schur and support arguments supplied analytically.
findings.central_dependency: Theorem 34 exactness and safety of its printed low-rank optimization; Remark 36 needs the corrected one-step formulation.
findings.consequence: A claimed safe output can be unsafe; this is not solely conservative loss.
findings.supported_correction: Use M²I in the block and M²Tr(eta1) in the dual. Alternatively, for k≥1 the exact support is M||h||₂||x||₂, attained by a rank-one matrix, giving an SOCP with both initial-state and robust-transition inequalities.
findings.boundary_cases: Zero h or x immediate. M=1 conceals the scaling defect. The source explicitly allows M>=0, so M=0 is already within its stated scope; handle the singleton prior {0} directly because the displayed strict primal feasibility argument fails at M=0. For the actual prior, closure under positive powers when M<=1 remains valid.
findings.counterevidence: Sparse and permutation formulations independently checked positively; the rank cap does not improve this particular rank-one support objective.
findings.epistemic_status: Established counterexample for the exact acquired version; no journal-final equivalence asserted.

findings.title: The printed infinite-horizon demonstration prior has only the origin robustly safe

source_location.statement: Section 5.5.1, program (22), Figure 6(a), and dependent Section 7.1/Figure 9

findings.claim_scope: The printed prior has stable members and admits the reported full-dimensional degree-four robust invariant certificate.
findings.hypotheses_checked: The exact printed prior A11=A22=1/2, A12,A21≥0, A12+A21=9/5 and compact triangular S are retained; 9/5 was confirmed in actual source images. Both witnesses belong to this prior.
findings.proof: A=[[1/2,9/10],[9/10,1/2]] and B=[[1/2,36/25],[9/25,1/2]] have independent left eigenvectors v=(1,1), w=(1,2), with eigenvalues 7/5 and 61/50. Bounded orbits in S force vᵀx=wᵀx=0, hence the common infinite-horizon safe set is exactly {0}. At A, vᵀ(Q−AQAᵀ)v=(1−49/25)vᵀQv≤0 contradicts the strict positive Lyapunov margin of (22a), so no degree can certify the stated input. Section 7.1 imports the same prior and allows g=0, carrying the obstruction to every nonnegative gamma. Its displayed A-star has off-diagonal sum9/10, inconsistent with9/5.
findings.decisive_calculation: Native linear exact fractions verified prior membership, both eigenvector equations, independent linear constraints and negative Lyapunov factor. The all-degree impossibility follows analytically.
findings.central_dependency: The specified numerical demonstration and its dependent nonlinear example; not the abstract conditional Theorems18/29.
findings.consequence: The claimed full-dimensional certificate and figures cannot correspond to the printed uncertainty set.
findings.supported_correction: Identify the actual intended and executed prior, and provide a matching certificate and figures. A possible alternative a+b=c with3/4<c<1 has stable individual matrices but unstable endpoint switching products; c=9/10 gives individual bound19/20 and product characteristic value−99/400 at1.
findings.boundary_cases: The alternative family is a mathematically valid candidate, not a certified intended typo correction or reproduced degree-four solution.
findings.counterevidence: Theorems18/29 assume stability and are not refuted by an input violating that premise. The distinct Section5.5.2 Frobenius-ball prior is individually stable by independent determinant/trace bounds; its experimental costs were not rerun.
findings.epistemic_status: Established contradiction of the printed demonstration; actual author execution remains unknown.

findings.title: Changing disturbance bounds can make the exact conditioned safe set nonconvex

source_location.statement: Remark27 and its noisy one-step SOCP

findings.claim_scope: Exactness for the uncertainty conditioned jointly on all observed states and disturbances, as distinct from a rectangular outer uncertainty model.
findings.hypotheses_checked: n=1, S=[−1,1], known linear A=0, gamma=3/4, d=0, p=1. Safe observations at−1/2 and1/2 have output0, past bounds W1=W2=1/4 and actual disturbance0. Next bound W3=1/2 is allowed to change.
findings.proof: At either sampled point, consistency implies |g|≤1/4, so all next outputs have magnitude≤3/4. For any other z, set N(t)=(t²−1/4)² and g_z(t)=(3/4)N(t)/(N(t)+(t−z)²). Its denominator never vanishes, it is smooth and bounded by3/4, vanishes at both samples, and equals3/4 at z. With next noise1/2 it sends z to5/4 outside S. Thus the exact next safe set is {−1/2,1/2}. The displayed program uses gamma+W3=5/4 at all states; nonnegative residual dual terms cannot reduce it, so its projection is empty.
findings.decisive_calculation: Native nonlinear exact arithmetic checked safe-history bounds and a smooth midpoint witness; the analytic g_z family proves the assertion at every unobserved state.
findings.central_dependency: Remark27's full-information exactness interpretation; its sufficient safety and the noiseless Theorem26 survive.
findings.consequence: A convex SOCP projection cannot represent this exact nonconvex conditioned set and can discard all actually safe sampled states.
findings.supported_correction: Identify the program as exact for U_k,A×U_0,g and a safe inner approximation for full-history uncertainty; or combine the unobserved-state program with finitely many conditioned feasibility checks at sampled states, retaining the joint constraints.
findings.boundary_cases: Constant or nonincreasing disturbance bounds remove this particular old-sample obstruction for robustly collected histories. No failure of the noise-only formula or general conservative safety is alleged.
findings.counterevidence: The additive plus sign before the future disturbance was verified at original image detail; no missing-sign finding. In a valid noiseless robust history, sampled points remain in the Theorem26 program.
findings.epistemic_status: Established counterexample to full-conditioned exactness under the stated changing bounds, with the alternative rectangular-model interpretation explicitly retained.

findings.title: A common affine translation can destroy the offline basis
findings.claim_scope: The prescribed mixtures of a safe basis and a minimizing state always remain a basis and permit inversion of the query matrix.
findings.hypotheses_checked: n=1, S=[−1,1], U0=[0,1], true A=1/2, nonnegative affine cost c(x)=x+1. The constant does not affect minimization; x-star=−1, z1=1 and epsilon=1/2 satisfy the stated choices.
findings.proof: The sole mixed query is0, so X is singular and all data leave U0 unchanged. In general, for invertible Z and s=eᵀZ⁻¹x-star, det X=epsilon^n det Z(1+(1−epsilon)s/epsilon). There is at most one exceptional positive epsilon; the scalar choice epsilon=1/4 succeeds.
findings.decisive_calculation: Root exact arithmetic verified singularity, unchanged uncertainty and a repaired query.
findings.central_dependency: The secondary offline baseline and the interpretation of its limiting optimum.
findings.consequence: An allowed implementation can request an undefined inverse. The limiting minimum-cost value can be only an infimum: with S=[0,1] and c=x every identifying query is positive despite infimum0.
findings.supported_correction: Check rank and choose a different positive epsilon when needed; state the epsilon-to-zero cost as an infimum unless attained.
findings.boundary_cases: Arbitrarily small nonexceptional epsilon values exist. Algorithm1 perturbs a point in the current span toward an outside point and does not share this collapse.
findings.counterevidence: No failure of the online independence argument or of any specific reported fixed-epsilon experiment is established.
findings.epistemic_status: Established local algorithmic defect with a bounded repair.

findings.title: Horizon monotonicity needs a fixed prediction target

source_location.statement: General learning definition and horizon comparison; Definitions4 and39

findings.claim_scope: Learning for horizonT automatically implies learning for a smaller horizon when the prediction objective is evaluated over the true horizon-dependent safe set.
findings.hypotheses_checked: S=[0,1]², R=[[0,−1],[1,0]], true f(x)=Rx, U0=conv{−I,R}, tolerance1/2. The comparison uses the paper's prediction-domain target, not global matrix identification.
findings.proof: True S¹(R)={(a,0):0≤a≤1}, whereas S²(R)={0}. All candidates fix0, so the two-step prediction target is met with no observations. Because−I is allowed, the only common one-step safe query is0 and the posterior never changes. At e1 in the true one-step safe set, R e1 and−e1 differ bysqrt(2)>1/2. One-step prediction learning is impossible.
findings.decisive_calculation: Root exact finite matrix calculation checked the witness and candidate-output gap; the no-information argument is analytic.
findings.central_dependency: The general definitional comparison; not the specialized singleton-identification Theorem8.
findings.consequence: Shrinking the target domain with horizon invalidates the asserted implication.
findings.supported_correction: Fix a horizon-independent prediction domain, or restrict the assertion to full parameter identification with the same target.
findings.boundary_cases: No claim is made that the full matrix is identifiable from two-step data in this example.
findings.counterevidence: Under Definitions4/39 a safe longer trajectory can be decomposed into shorter observations without changing the identification target; that interpretation survives.
findings.epistemic_status: Established scope counterexample with explicit distinction of learning targets.

findings.title: The entrywise maximum is not preserved by Schur conjugation
findings.claim_scope: The uniform power bound uses the entrywise maximum of the original matrices to bound entries after unitary Schur triangularization.
findings.hypotheses_checked: A singleton compact stable prior is enough; the positive-radius witness has R=1/10<1 and entrywise maximum M=11/10.
findings.proof: For A=[[11/10,1],[−1,−9/10]], the printed exponent-one bound squared is2(R+M)²=72/25. On v=(1,1), ||Av||²/||v||²=401/100>72/25. The executed nilpotent companion N=[[1,1],[−1,−1]] has norm2 but printed bound sqrt(2). Unitary conjugation preserves the spectral norm, not the entrywise maximum.
findings.decisive_calculation: Native linear run checked the nilpotent witness; the positive-R witness and general repaired bound were checked analytically without a duplicate run.
findings.central_dependency: A local estimate in Lemma24's uniform-decay proof and the ensuing SOS existence argument.
findings.consequence: The displayed inequality is false, but the lemma's needed uniform decay remains valid.
findings.supported_correction: Replace M by max||A||₂ or by nM. Alternatively, use compactness, pointwise powers of norm below1, a finite neighborhood cover and bounded remainders to obtain uniform decay, then the finite polynomial Lyapunov sum.
findings.boundary_cases: If R=0 every n-by-n matrix is nilpotent of index at mostn; for0<R<1 the corrected polynomial-times-exponential bound decays.
findings.counterevidence: The conditional existence theorem is not disproved; a complete repair preserving its conclusion is supplied.
findings.epistemic_status: Established false local estimate, fully repairable.

findings.title: Two positive-radius arguments invert the Schur-complement factor
findings.claim_scope: The block [[beta I,x],[xᵀ,1/2]] is PSD on a ball of squared radius1/(2 beta).
findings.hypotheses_checked: beta>0, with example beta=1/4 and x=1; compatible preceding linear choices Q=1 and alpha=2 give Q/alpha=1/2>beta.
findings.proof: The actual Schur condition is ||x||²≤beta/2. The printed ball includes x=1 but the block determinant is−7/8; the resulting membership block in the preceding construction has determinant−1/2.
findings.decisive_calculation: One native linear exact Schur calculation supports both occurrences. Nonlinear and root work reuse those unchanged results with original execution attribution.
findings.central_dependency: Local interior-ball steps in conditional full-dimensionality proofs.
findings.consequence: The stated quantitative ball inclusion is false; the existence of a positive-radius ball remains true.
findings.supported_correction: Use radius sqrt(beta/2). It stays positive, and the added constant PSD block is an SOS matrix without increasing degree.
findings.boundary_cases: No universal numerical size is asserted; beta is strictly positive under the existing construction.
findings.counterevidence: Both full-dimensionality conclusions survive the corrected radius.
findings.epistemic_status: Established local reciprocal error, not a refutation of the conditional main theorems.

findings.title: Optimization selections require explicit existence and empty-set handling
findings.claim_scope: Literal optimizer and coordinate-extrema selections are available under the printed hypotheses.
findings.hypotheses_checked: Theorem8 permits arbitrary cost on a polyhedral S; the earlier nonnegative-cost convention is treated as an alternative hypothesis, not silently omitted. Section4 imposes no compactness of S.
findings.proof: For S=R,U0=[0,1],A-star=1/2,c=1 the minimum of x is unbounded although query1 identifies. Imposing global nonnegative cost excludes this instance and narrows arbitrary-c wording. S=[1,2],U0=[2,3] has an empty common one-step safe set and requires an explicit impossible branch. Independently, with S=R and ellipsoidal priorU0=[−1,1], the two-step safe set isR and full-dimensional but the coordinate maximum/minimum used in Lemma12 do not exist.
findings.decisive_calculation: Analytic scalar feasibility and unboundedness checks; no optimization run is claimed.
findings.central_dependency: Implementation of finite/measurable selections in Algorithms1/3 and the sampling construction.
findings.consequence: Some literal steps are undefined without an additional hypothesis or fallback, even though identifying trajectories or full-dimensional safe sets can exist.
findings.supported_correction: Handle empty safe sets; impose compact S where appropriate or use finite-cost/feasible-point rank fallbacks and a bounded slice retaining an interior ball; make randomized selections measurable.
findings.boundary_cases: A finite lower-bounded linear objective on a nonempty polyhedron attains its minimum; the issue is not general nonattainment for such LPs.
findings.counterevidence: The information/span impossibility theorem and generic algebraic rank argument remain supported when the selections are well-defined.
findings.epistemic_status: Established implementation/hypothesis qualification with explicit counterevidence and repair.
